subject: Latency spike impacting Fenwick AI - coordination + customer message
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [Alert] High latency spike affecting Fenwick AI (us-west-2)

Team,

Monitoring flagged a sudden latency/throughput regression impacting Fenwick AI (deal DW-4721) in us-west-2 starting ~09:05 PST. Key observations attached (initial-metrics-snapshot.png):
- 95th pct latency jumped from ~110ms to ~1.2s between 09:05–09:10.
- Overall throughput dropped ~28%; concurrent request queue increased.
- No HTTP 5xx surge, but token generation tail latency is elevated.

I’m spinning up a triage channel but wanted core owners tagged. Immediate asks:
1) Dev: quick triage to identify whether this is model runtime (KV cache, kernel) or infra (batching, workers).
2) Eng/SRE: if mitigation available (pin model, scale, restart workers), call it out and estimate ETA.
3) Sales/CS: prepare a short customer note if this persists beyond 30m. I’ve attached the snapshot + a timeline stub.

Attachments: initial-metrics-snapshot.png (PNG, 24KB), incident-timeline.csv (CSV, 6KB)

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Alert] High latency spike affecting Fenwick AI (us-west-2)

On Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 09:12 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Monitoring flagged a sudden latency/throughput regression impacting Fenwick AI...

Quick triage results (observed at 09:25):
- Root cause hypothesis: a recent model rollout triggered a KV cache miss storm on the large LLM variant. We see a correlated rise in cache fill rate + longer KV warming sequences per request.
- Evidence: spike in KV cache churn and a small number of workers with >2x GPU memory allocation compared to baseline.

Immediate mitigations I’m initiating now (ETA ~20–30m):
1) Pin Fenwick's tenant routing to previous stable model binary (v2.11) for incoming sessions — config push in progress.
2) Reduce batch window from 40ms -> 20ms for the affected GPU pool to cut tail-latency impact.
3) Trigger rolling restart of 6 inference-worker pods in us-west-2 (graceful, one-by-one).

I recommend we hold external messaging for ~30m until we confirm tail latency is back to baseline; otherwise we risk sending premature info. I’ll post updates every 20m or on major state changes.

Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fenwick.ai>, ops@fenwick.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Incident — Draft customer note (Fenwick AI)

Jane / Fenwick Ops,

We detected a performance regression this morning that may have affected API response times for a subset of requests between ~09:05–09:40 PST. Our SRE and engineering teams are actively mitigating; we expect to have a full update within 60–90 minutes.

Customer-facing draft (please confirm receipt; we will not send until we validate mitigations):
-----
Hi Jane,
We’ve identified a transient issue impacting inference latency for some requests this morning (09:05–09:40 PST). Our team applied a mitigation that has reduced tail latency; we are continuing to monitor and will follow up with a full incident report and any recommended configuration changes. No customer data exposure or integrity issue is associated with this event.
Estimated next update: within 90 minutes.
Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize a detailed postmortem.
Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
-----

Internal note: Attached is the customer-communication-draft.txt (sendable copy). Marissa, please advise on tone and whether to offer credits or an SLA exception if Fenwick insists.

Attachments: customer-communication-draft.txt (TXT, 1.2KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Incident — Draft customer note (Fenwick AI)

Sean —
Thanks for the draft. My suggested tweaks to keep the message concise and action-oriented:
- Lead with confirmation of mitigation (if we have it) and then call out the timeline and next steps.
- Explicitly state "no data loss" as you have, and add a line offering a technical debrief if they want it.
- Reserve credits/SLA exceptions as a follow-up item after the postmortem; flag to CS leadership for approval.

Suggested short copy (send only after Dev confirms mitigation complete):
-----
Hi Jane,
We experienced a transient increase in inference latency between ~09:05–09:40 PST this morning affecting a subset of requests. Our engineering team implemented a mitigation that has brought latency back toward normal; we are continuing to monitor and will provide a full incident report within 3 business days. No customer data was exposed. If you’d like a technical debrief, we can schedule one with our engineering team.
Best,
Sean Gallagher
-----

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@fenwick.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update: mitigation applied, monitoring stable

Update and timeline (finalized):
- 13:05 PST: Detect continued elevated tail latency after initial mitigations.
- 13:20 PST: Dev pinned Fenwick routing to v2.11 and reduced batch window.
- 13:30 PST: Rolling restart of 6 inference workers initiated (completed 13:45 PST).
- 13:55 PST: 95th pct latency returned to baseline (~120ms); throughput normalized.

We’ve attached incident-timeline.csv with timestamps and operator actions. Next steps:
1) Short postmortem scheduled (RCA prep) — owner: Dev Patel, draft due EOD next business day.
2) Engineering action items: add KV cache smoothing and a temporary rate limiter for high-cardinality prefixes (Dev to estimate effort).
3) Product decision: evaluate canary rollback safeguards to prevent similar rollout-triggered cache storms (Jonas / Hannah to scope).

Customer communication status: Sean/Marissa — send the updated short copy now if you think the tone is acceptable. We will flag in the postmortem whether an SLA credit is warranted.

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (CSV, 9KB)

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
